chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
It is inscribed upon the door of Paradise: 'Charity is [rewarded] with ten, and the loan is with eighteen.' And in another report, 'fifteen'.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in reward between charity and lending money in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a quantitative hierarchy of reward, positioning the loan (qarḍ) as superior to general charity (ṣadaqah) with a reward of eighteen or fifteen compared to ten. In Shia scholarly tradition, this distinction underscores the virtue of relieving specific burdens and fostering social solidarity through interest-free lending, which is often viewed as a more sustained act of benevolence than one-time almsgiving. The variation in numbers reflects the nuanced understanding of different degrees of need and the sincerity of the lender.
